The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput and latency under varying sequence lengths. To establish a reliable benchmark, the test utilizes a fixed prompt size to isolate the decode-phase performance within the benchmark. This benchmark measures tokens per second (TPS) across multiple GPU configurations to ensure the benchmark results are reproducible. 

In this benchmark, memory bandwidth serves as the primary bottleneck for the decode benchmark. As the benchmark progresses, the KV cache utilization is monitored to assess how the benchmark scales with increasing context windows. A high-performance benchmark must account for batch size variations, as the benchmark efficiency shifts from compute-bound to memory-bound regimes. 

The benchmark data indicates that the Gemma B70 architecture optimizes the decode benchmark by leveraging efficient attention mechanisms. Consequently, the benchmark shows improved stability in long-context scenarios. Every benchmark iteration validates the precision of the quantization method used in the benchmark. Ultimately, this benchmark provides a standardized metric for comparing the Gemma B70 decode benchmark against other large language models in the same benchmark category.
